89:3.en: And [by] the even [number] and the odd

89:4.en: And [by] the night when it passes

89:5.ar: هَلۡ فِي ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمࣱ لِّذِي حِجۡرٍ
89:5.en: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception

89:6.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
89:6.en: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad

89:8.ar: ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
89:8.en: The likes of whom had never been created in the land

89:9.en: And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley

89:10.en: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes

89:11.en: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands

89:13.en: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment

89:14.en: Indeed, your Lord is in observation

89:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
89:15.en: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me

89:17.en: No! But you do not honor the orphan

89:18.en: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor

89:19.ar: وَتَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكۡلࣰ ا لَّمࣰّ ا
89:19.en: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether

89:20.ar: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلۡمَالَ حُبࣰّ ا جَمࣰّ ا
89:20.en: And you love wealth with immense love

89:21.ar: كَلَّآۖ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ دَكࣰّ ا دَكࣰّ ا
89:21.en: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed

89:22.ar: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفࣰّ ا صَفࣰّ ا
89:22.en: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance

89:24.en: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life

89:25.en: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment

89:26.en: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers]

89:27.en: [To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul

89:28.en: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]

IaQr_Nu9CRA.speaker: adnan
IaQr_Nu9CRA.speaker_note: presents his own categorization of Juz Amma, which he says he worked on through his university thesis
IaQr_Nu9CRA.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Fajr
IaQr_Nu9CRA.one_line: Al-Fajr gives the believer a correct perspective on life: ease and hardship are both tests, never signs of Allah's love or contempt.
IaQr_Nu9CRA.summary: He places Al-Fajr in his grouping of Juz Amma as the fourth of the tools that only faith provides: a proper perspective for explaining what happens to us. The surah opens with oaths by opposites, dawn and long nights, even and odd, night passing into day, because life is a series of opposites. It then recalls Aad, Thamud and Pharaoh, who were given everyone's dream of power and wealth and still destroyed, raising the question of whether those gifts were good for them. The core is two verses: the person given plenty says his Lord honoured him, the person whose provision is tightened says his Lord humiliated him, and both are wrong. The shared word is that Allah tested each of them. Nothing personal is implied, and nothing arrives labelled good or bad; we attach the labels by what we do with it. He carefully separates what is simply dealt to us from the consequences of our own choices, which we must own. The surah then names the real problem: not honouring orphans, not feeding the poor, and devouring wealth with endless greed, when sharing our surplus of money, time and attention would solve much of the world's need. Everything is crushed on the Last Day, and the soul at peace, which understood life as tests, is invited into Paradise.

outline.heading: His categorization of the Quran's surahs
outline.gist: He explains that the grouping he uses is his own long work; scholars had other takes and listeners may disagree with the divisions.

outline.heading: The groups of Juz Amma: fundamentals, choices, tools of faith
outline.gist: After the fundamentals and the surahs on choice comes a group giving tools that only faith can generate; lose the faith and you lose the tools.

outline.heading: The fourth tool: a proper perspective on the world
outline.gist: A believer needs a correct way of explaining events to himself and others, a tool not to be taken lightly.

outline.heading: Oaths by opposites: dawn, ten nights, even and odd, the passing night
outline.gist: Allah swears by opposites and by one opposite turning into another, which points to the surah's theme.

outline.heading: Aad, Iram and Thamud: unmatched strength
outline.gist: No nation was like them in their region; 'did you not see' can mean trusted knowledge, which equals seeing. Thamud carved rock in the valleys.

outline.heading: Pharaoh of the stakes and the corruption of all three
outline.gist: The stakes are likely the pyramids, possibly the banners of a great army; all three nations multiplied corruption and were struck with punishment.

outline.heading: Why the stories: were their gifts good or bad for them?
outline.gist: They had everyone's dream of wealth, power and status, yet were destroyed; whether it was good depended on what they did with it.

outline.heading: The honoured man: 'my Lord has honoured me'
outline.gist: Given wealth and pleasure, a person concludes God must love him and that his choices were right.

outline.heading: The restricted man: 'my Lord has humiliated me'
outline.gist: Someone always barely making ends meet concludes God despises him; both conclusions are wrong.

outline.heading: Life swings between opposites
outline.gist: Our hearts move like a barometer between getting and not getting what we want, which is why the surah opened with opposites.

outline.heading: The shared word: Allah tested him
outline.gist: Both verses say Allah tested the person; ease or hardship carries no message about your worth.

outline.heading: What is dealt to you versus what you caused
outline.gist: The verses concern what you had no hand in; a speeding driver on his phone or a heavy smoker must own the consequences, unlike the careful driver or the non-smoking runner with cancer.

outline.heading: Good and bad are understood the same way
outline.gist: Both are tests: ease calls for gratitude and helping others, hardship for perseverance.

outline.heading: The tyrants were given everything and failed; this tool brings calm
outline.gist: Their power did not mean they were loved; whoever holds this understanding lives a calm life, and every Muslim should be taught it.

outline.heading: The believer's affair is always good
outline.gist: The Prophet described the believer who thanks Allah in good times and perseveres in bad, turning both into good.

outline.heading: Nothing comes from the heavens labelled
outline.gist: Ease and difficulty arrive unlabelled; we stamp them good or evil, and what we most wanted can become the worst thing that happened to us.

outline.heading: The real problem: the orphan and the poor
outline.gist: The issue is how we live: not honouring the orphan, who is socially in need, nor urging the feeding of the poor, who are financially in need.

outline.heading: Give your surplus: money, skills, time, a listening ear
outline.gist: If everyone shared what is extra, most problems would fade; often people need attention or someone to talk to more than money, and Ramadan is the time for zakat.

outline.heading: Devouring wealth with endless greed
outline.gist: Consuming inheritance greedily and loving wealth intensely is the problem; there is enough for everyone's needs but not for everyone's greed.

outline.heading: The earth pounded flat; the Lord comes with angels in rows
outline.gist: Everything we own disappears and none of it, not even titles, goes with us; then Allah comes in His glory with the angels.

outline.heading: How simple life really was
outline.gist: Life was just tests to meet with gratitude or perseverance; being alive is already evidence of Allah's love.

outline.heading: 'I wish I had prepared for my life'
outline.gist: On that day people realize the Hereafter is the real, permanent life shaped by their choices, and no one punishes or binds as Allah does.

outline.heading: The soul at peace returns well-pleased and well-pleasing
outline.gist: The one who understood life stayed calm through good and bad, and is invited to join Allah's servants and enter His Paradise.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: His thematic grouping of Juz Amma into fundamentals, choices and tools of faith.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Ease and hardship are both tests with nothing personal in them; only our response gives them meaning.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Distinguish what is dealt to you from consequences you caused and must own and repent for.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Ease calls for gratitude and hardship for perseverance; the believer turns both into good.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: This perspective is what gives a calm, settled life.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Share surplus money, skills and time with the socially and financially needy.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Greed and love of possessions, not scarcity, cause most of the world's need.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Everything is crushed, the real life begins, and the tranquil soul is welcomed into Paradise.

hadith.gist: Amazing is the affair of the believer: when good comes he is grateful and when harm comes he perseveres, and both are good for him

maxims: Nothing comes from the heavens labelled
It's not personal; it's just your test
We label what we're given
Enough for our needs, not enough for our greed
You are alive: that is evidence He loves you

stories.point: They had the greatest power and wealth, which did not mean Allah loved them; they failed their test
The careless driver bears the consequence of his choices; the careful one has simply been tested

stories.who: A non-smoking marathon runner with lung cancer
stories.point: Contrasted with a heavy smoker: one illness is a test, the other a consequence to own

takeaways: Do not read your wealth or poverty as a verdict on how Allah sees you
Meet ease with gratitude and giving, and hardship with perseverance
Own the consequences of your own mistakes instead of calling them tests
Share your surplus of money, time, skills and attention with those in need
Keep the Hereafter in view as the real life your choices are shaping

38:1.en: Sad. By the Qur'an containing reminder

38:2.ar: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي عِزَّةࣲ وَشِقَاقࣲ‏
38:2.en: But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension

38:3.ar: كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن قَرۡنࣲ فَنَادَواْ وَّلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصࣲ‏
38:3.en: How many a generation have We destroyed before them, and they [then] called out; but it was not a time for escape

38:4.ar: وَعَجِبُوٓاْ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا سَٰحِرࣱ كَذَّابٌ
38:4.en: And they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, "This is a magician and a liar

38:5.ar: أَجَعَلَ ٱلۡأٓلِهَةَ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدًاۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءٌ عُجَابࣱ‏
38:5.en: Has he made the gods [only] one God? Indeed, this is a curious thing

38:6.ar: وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِنۡهُمۡ أَنِ ٱمۡشُواْ وَٱصۡبِرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِكُمۡۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءࣱ يُرَادُ
38:6.en: And the eminent among them went forth, [saying], "Continue, and be patient over [the defense of] your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended

38:7.ar: مَا سَمِعۡنَا بِهَٰذَا فِي ٱلۡمِلَّةِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخۡتِلَٰقٌ
38:7.en: We have not heard of this in the latest religion. This is not but a fabrication

38:8.ar: أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلذِّكۡرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ فِي شَكࣲّ مِّن ذِكۡرِيۚ بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ
38:8.en: Has the message been revealed to him out of [all of] us?" Rather, they are in doubt about My message. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment

38:9.ar: أَمۡ عِندَهُمۡ خَزَآئِنُ رَحۡمَةِ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡوَهَّابِ
38:9.en: Or do they have the depositories of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower

38:10.ar: أَمۡ لَهُم مُّلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ فَلۡيَرۡتَقُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَسۡبَٰبِ
38:10.en: Or is theirs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [any] ways of access

38:11.ar: جُندࣱ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهۡزُومࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابِ
38:11.en: [They are but] soldiers [who will be] defeated there among the companies [of disbelievers]

38:12.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ وَعَادࣱ وَفِرۡعَوۡنُ ذُو ٱلۡأَوۡتَادِ
38:12.en: The people of Noah denied before them, and [the tribe of] 'Aad and Pharaoh, the owner of stakes

38:13.ar: وَثَمُودُ وَقَوۡمُ لُوطࣲ وَأَصۡحَٰبُ لۡـَٔيۡكَةِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابُ
38:13.en: And [the tribe of] Thamud and the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket. Those are the companies

38:14.ar: إِن كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقَابِ
38:14.en: Each of them denied the messengers, so My penalty was justified

38:15.ar: وَمَا يَنظُرُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقࣲ‏
38:15.en: And these [disbelievers] await not but one blast [of the Horn]; for it there will be no delay

38:16.ar: وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا قَبۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:16.en: And they say, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share [of the punishment] before the Day of Account

38:17.ar: ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:17.en: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]

38:18.ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ
38:18.en: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, exalting [Allah] in the [late] afternoon and [after] sunrise

38:19.en: And the birds were assembled, all with him repeating [praises]

38:20.ar: وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:20.en: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech

38:21.ar: ۞وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ
38:21.en: And has there come to you the news of the adversaries, when they climbed over the wall of [his] prayer chamber

38:22.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡهُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
38:22.en: When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them? They said, "Fear not. [We are] two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not exceed [it] and guide us to the sound path

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; so he said, 'Entrust her to me,' and he overpowered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: [David] said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allah]

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: [We said], "O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allah." Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account

38:27.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا بَٰطِلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
38:27.en: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and that between them aimlessly. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire

38:28.ar: أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلۡفُجَّارِ
38:28.en: Or should we treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land? Or should We treat those who fear Allah like the wicked

38:29.ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ مُبَٰرَكࣱ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:29.en: [This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded

38:30.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لِدَاوُۥدَ سُلَيۡمَٰنَۚ نِعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:30.en: And to David We gave Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah]

38:31.ar: إِذۡ عُرِضَ عَلَيۡهِ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّٰفِنَٰتُ ٱلۡجِيَادُ
38:31.en: [Mention] when there were exhibited before him in the afternoon the poised [standing] racehorses

38:32.ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَحۡبَبۡتُ حُبَّ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ عَن ذِكۡرِ رَبِّي حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتۡ بِٱلۡحِجَابِ
38:32.en: And he said, "Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good [things] over the remembrance of my Lord until the sun disappeared into the curtain [of darkness]

38:33.ar: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّۖ فَطَفِقَ مَسۡحَۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَاقِ
38:33.en: [He said], "Return them to me," and set about striking [their] legs and necks

38:34.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا سُلَيۡمَٰنَ وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا عَلَىٰ كُرۡسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
38:34.en: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he returned

38:35.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَهَبۡ لِي مُلۡكࣰ ا لَّا يَنۢبَغِي لِأَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
38:35.en: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower

38:36.ar: فَسَخَّرۡنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجۡرِي بِأَمۡرِهِۦ رُخَآءً حَيۡثُ أَصَابَ
38:36.en: So We subjected to him the wind blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed

38:37.en: And [also] the devils [of jinn] - every builder and diver

38:38.en: And others bound together in shackles

38:39.ar: هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمۡنُنۡ أَوۡ أَمۡسِكۡ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
38:39.en: [We said], "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account

38:40.ar: وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:40.en: And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return

38:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِنُصۡبࣲ وَعَذَابٍ
38:41.en: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment

38:42.ar: ٱرۡكُضۡ بِرِجۡلِكَۖ هَٰذَا مُغۡتَسَلُۢ بَارِدࣱ وَشَرَابࣱ‏
38:42.en: [So he was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink

38:43.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهۡلَهُۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:43.en: And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah]

38:45.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلۡأَيۡدِي وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
38:45.en: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - those of strength and [religious] vision

38:46.en: Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the home [of the Hereafter]

38:47.en: And indeed they are, to Us, among the chosen and outstanding

38:48.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلۡيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِۖ وَكُلࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَخۡيَارِ
38:48.en: And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding

38:49.ar: هَٰذَا ذِكۡرࣱۚ وَإِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:49.en: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return

38:50.en: Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors will be opened to them

38:51.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا يَدۡعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَٰكِهَةࣲ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَشَرَابࣲ‏
38:51.en: Reclining within them, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink

38:52.en: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances and of equal age

38:53.en: This is what you, [the righteous], are promised for the Day of Account

38:54.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَرِزۡقُنَا مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ
38:54.en: Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no depletion

38:55.en: This [is so]. But indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return

38:56.en: Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the resting place

38:57.en: This - so let them taste it - is scalding water and [foul] purulence

38:58.en: And other [punishments] of its type [in various] kinds

38:59.ar: هَٰذَا فَوۡجࣱ مُّقۡتَحِمࣱ مَّعَكُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِهِمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ
38:59.en: [Its inhabitants will say], "This is a company bursting in with you. No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire

38:60.ar: قَالُواْ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِكُمۡۖ أَنتُمۡ قَدَّمۡتُمُوهُ لَنَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡقَرَارُ
38:60.en: They will say, "Nor you! No welcome for you. You, [our leaders], brought this upon us, and wretched is the settlement

38:61.ar: قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَٰذَا فَزِدۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا ضِعۡفࣰ ا فِي ٱلنَّارِ
38:61.en: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase for him double punishment in the Fire

38:62.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَىٰ رِجَالࣰ ا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَشۡرَارِ
38:62.en: And they will say, "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst

38:63.ar: أَتَّخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ سِخۡرِيًّا أَمۡ زَاغَتۡ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ
38:63.en: Is it [because] we took them in ridicule, or has [our] vision turned away from them

38:64.ar: إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَحَقࣱّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهۡلِ ٱلنَّارِ
38:64.en: Indeed, that is truth - the quarreling of the people of the Fire

38:71.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَٰلِقُۢ بَشَرࣰ ا مِّن طِينࣲ‏
38:71.en: [So mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay

38:72.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
38:72.en: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration

38:73.en: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely

38:74.ar: إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
38:74.en: Except Iblees; he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers

38:75.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَيَّۖ أَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ أَمۡ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَالِينَ
38:75.en: [Allah] said, "O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant [then], or were you [already] among the haughty

38:76.ar: قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡهُ خَلَقۡتَنِي مِن نَّارࣲ وَخَلَقۡتَهُۥ مِن طِينࣲ‏
38:76.en: He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay

38:77.en: [Allah] said, "Then get out of Paradise, for indeed, you are expelled

38:78.ar: وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكَ لَعۡنَتِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ
38:78.en: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense

38:79.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرۡنِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
38:79.en: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected

38:80.en: [Allah] said, "So indeed, you are of those reprieved

38:81.en: Until the Day of the time well-known

38:82.en: [Iblees] said, "By your might, I will surely mislead them all

38:83.en: Except, among them, Your chosen servants

38:84.en: [Allah] said, "The truth [is My oath], and the truth I say

38:85.ar: لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
38:85.en: [That] I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them that follow you all together

38:86.ar: قُلۡ مَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرࣲ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَكَلِّفِينَ
38:86.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "I do not ask you for the Qur'an any payment, and I am not of the pretentious

38:87.en: It is but a reminder to the worlds

38:88.en: And you will surely know [the truth of] its information after a time

159GS6n3mj4.speaker: adnan
159GS6n3mj4.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at MWN, his usual cluster framing and voice throughout
159GS6n3mj4.title: Surat Sad Summary
159GS6n3mj4.one_line: Surah Sad as a lesson in acknowledging mistakes and returning to the truth, through Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub and the refusal of Iblis.
159GS6n3mj4.summary: He places Surah Sad in a cluster of surahs about submission to Allah and reads it as a surah about one trait: admitting a mistake and returning to what is right without shame. The opening verses diagnose disbelief not as disagreement but as pride and stubborn clinging to error, shown in the Quraysh leaders who reject the message simply because it is new, as earlier nations did. He then walks through the prophets in the surah. Dawud, a king, judge and prophet, rules after hearing only one litigant, and although he could have blamed the intruders who climbed into his private place of worship, he immediately seeks forgiveness; the lesson is that anyone who judges must hear the other side, and this is where the word khalifah enters the human job description. Sulayman admits that love of his horses delayed his prayer, and he rejects the story that he slaughtered them. Ayyub, after years of patience, is corrected for an oath against his wife. Each looks at his own fault, not at others'. The people of Hell wonder why certain sinners are missing: they returned to Allah at some point. Iblis is the counterexample who knew he was wrong and stayed. He asks listeners to make returning to the truth part of who they are.

outline.heading: Surah Sad: returning to the truth even against yourself
outline.gist: The surah's message is submission through acknowledging mistakes and going back to righteousness without embarrassment, a trait of both Muslims and good human beings.

outline.heading: Bal: the real cause of disbelief is pride and stubbornness
outline.gist: The particle bal signals that the stated reasons are not the real ones; the disbelievers are held back by self-importance and by insisting on staying in what they know is wrong.

outline.heading: Rejecting the message because it is new
outline.gist: The Quraysh leaders tell people to hold to their idols because nobody before ever said this; refusing something only because it is unfamiliar is part of the disease.

outline.heading: Earlier nations who refused their prophets the same way
outline.gist: The surah lists the people of Nuh, Lut, Shuayb and the confederates, who saw they were wrong yet refused, and warns Quraysh that the same outcome awaits.

outline.heading: Interlude
Dawud's many roles and the two intruders
outline.gist: Dawud was king, commander, prophet, artist and judge, and kept private time for worship; two disputants climb his wall and bring him the case of the 99 ewes and the one.

outline.heading: Judging after hearing one side
outline.gist: Dawud rules for the complainant without hearing the other man; whoever judges or takes a side is obliged to hear the other party however weak its case looks. He realizes, repents and is forgiven.

outline.heading: The khalifah: judging with truth, not desire
outline.gist: Allah names Dawud a khalifah and tells him to judge by truth and not follow desire; the word first appears in a surah about admitting error, a fitting place.

outline.heading: Creation has a purpose, so cling to the truth
outline.gist: The heavens and earth were not made in vain as the disbelievers think; those who return to the right are not equal to those who do not.

outline.heading: Dawud had every excuse and used none
outline.gist: It was his day off, they invaded his privacy and they were angels testing him, yet he did not rationalize or punish them; he simply admitted his mistake, the mark of those close to Allah.

outline.heading: Sulayman's horses and the delayed prayer
outline.gist: Sulayman's love of fine horses delayed his prayer until sunset; he admits it openly.

outline.heading: Rejecting the claim that he slaughtered the horses
outline.gist: The verb means stroking the horses, not killing them; the slaughter story comes from Israelite reports that contradict the mercy of prophets and the point of the passage.

outline.heading: Forgetting inshallah and the trial of the child
outline.gist: Sulayman vowed to father sons who would all serve Allah without saying inshallah, then had one child born disabled, and again openly asked forgiveness.

outline.heading: Sulayman's dua for a unique kingdom
outline.gist: Kings who admit their mistakes can be trusted with power; he asks for a dominion like no other to show that strength can serve Allah, and it is granted.

outline.heading: Focus on your own mistakes, not other people's
outline.gist: The prophets in the surah all had power or hardship to blame, but they looked only at their own fault, because each person answers for his own actions.

outline.heading: Ayyub's oath against his wife
outline.gist: After years of illness and loss, Ayyub swears in anger to strike his wife for her complaint; once healed he is told to fulfill it with a handful of grass, a correction even for the most patient.

outline.heading: Awwab: the one who keeps returning
outline.gist: Allah praises Ayyub as an excellent servant who constantly returns; the quality the surah celebrates is returning, not never erring.

outline.heading: The people of Hell ask where the 'evil' people went
outline.gist: Those in Hell wonder why men they mocked as wrongdoers are missing; the answer is that those people at some point admitted their wrong and returned to Allah.

outline.heading: Iblis: the one who knew and did not return
outline.gist: Allah asks Iblis whether he is arrogant or truly higher; either way he could have admitted the mistake, but he insisted fire is better than clay and stayed with his error.

outline.heading: The Prophet claims no perfection, only return
outline.gist: The surah closes with the Prophet saying he asks no reward and pretends to be nothing he is not; the surah is a reminder whose importance people will learn later.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Returning to the right after a mistake, openly and without shame, is the trait the whole surah teaches through each prophet.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Disbelief is driven by pride and stubbornly staying in error, not by honest disagreement.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Iblis is the model of arrogance that refuses to retract a known mistake.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Anyone who judges or takes sides must hear the other party, however obvious one side seems.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Dawud refused to rationalize his mistake despite every excuse being available.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Focus on your own faults rather than others', since you answer only for yourself.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub each acknowledge a mistake openly.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: The khalifah role is defined by judging with truth and not desire; leaders who admit error can be trusted with power.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: He rejects Israelite reports that make Sulayman slaughter innocent horses as contrary to the character of prophets.

hadith.gist: Sulayman said he would father many sons who would all strive for Allah but did not say inshallah, and only one child was born, incomplete

maxims: Accept the truth even if it is against yourself
If you judge, you must hear the other side
Focus on what you are doing wrong, not others

stories.point: He judged after hearing one side, then admitted it at once despite every excuse.
He openly admitted that love of his horses delayed his prayer.
Even a small omission is acknowledged and repented.
Even after great patience he was corrected for mistreating his wife and given a way to make it right.
Knowing you are wrong and staying there is the most dangerous state.

takeaways: Admit mistakes openly when they are pointed out, without embarrassment
Do not rationalize your errors even when you have good excuses
Hear both sides before judging or taking a side in a dispute
Look at your own faults instead of other people's
Do not reject something only because it is new to you

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Certainly has Allah heard the speech of the one who argues with you, [O Muhammad], concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue; indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Those who pronounce thihar among you [to separate] from their wives - they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving

58:3.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:3.en: And those who pronounce thihar from their wives and then [wish to] go back on what they said - then [there must be] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished thereby; and Allah is Acquainted with what you do

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who does not find [a slave] - then a fast for two months consecutively before they touch one another; and he who is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allah and His Messenger; and those are the limits [set by] Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment

58:5.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ كُبِتُواْ كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ وَقَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَآ ءَايَٰتِۭ بَيِّنَٰتࣲۚ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:5.en: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased as those before them were abased. And We have certainly sent down verses of clear evidence. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment

58:6.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ أَحۡصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
58:6.en: On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah had enumerated it, while they forgot it; and Allah is, over all things, Witness

58:7.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمۡ وَلَا خَمۡسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كَانُواْۖ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
58:7.en: Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is in no private conversation three but that He is the fourth of them, nor are there five but that He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them [in knowledge] wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did, on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is, of all things, Knowing

58:8.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نُهُواْ عَنِ ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ وَيَتَنَٰجَوۡنَ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِۖ وَإِذَا جَآءُوكَ حَيَّوۡكَ بِمَا لَمۡ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ وَيَقُولُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَوۡلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا ٱللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُۚ حَسۡبُهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُ يَصۡلَوۡنَهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
58:8.en: Have you not considered those who were forbidden from private conversation, then they return to that which they were forbidden and converse among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that [word] by which Allah does not greet you and say among themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination

58:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَنَٰجَيۡتُمۡ فَلَا تَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ وَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
58:9.en: O you who have believed, when you converse privately, do not converse about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger but converse about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered

58:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ لِيَحۡزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيۡسَ بِضَآرِّهِمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
58:10.en: Private conversation is only from Satan that he may grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely

58:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمۡ تَفَسَّحُواْ فِي ٱلۡمَجَٰلِسِ فَٱفۡسَحُواْ يَفۡسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُواْ فَٱنشُزُواْ يَرۡفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ دَرَجَٰتࣲۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:11.en: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Space yourselves" in assemblies, then make space; Allah will make space for you. And when you are told, "Arise," then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do

58:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نَٰجَيۡتُمُ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ نَجۡوَىٰكُمۡ صَدَقَةࣰۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ وَأَطۡهَرُۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَجِدُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
58:12.en: O you who have believed, when you [wish to] privately consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you find not [the means] - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

58:13.ar: ءَأَشۡفَقۡتُمۡ أَن تُقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ نَجۡوَىٰكُمۡ صَدَقَٰتࣲۚ فَإِذۡ لَمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَتَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
58:13.en: Have you feared to present before your consultation charities? Then when you do not and Allah has forgiven you, then [at least] establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do

58:14.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ قَوۡمًا غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مَّا هُم مِّنكُمۡ وَلَا مِنۡهُمۡ وَيَحۡلِفُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡكَذِبِ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
58:14.en: Have you not considered those who make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to untruth while they know [they are lying]

58:15.ar: أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدًاۖ إِنَّهُمۡ سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
58:15.en: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, it was evil that they were doing

58:16.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَهُمۡ جُنَّةࣰ فَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:16.en: They took their [false] oaths as a cover, so they averted [people] from the way of Allah, and for them is a humiliating punishment

58:17.ar: لَّن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
58:17.en: Never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
58:18.en: On the Day Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you and think that they are [standing] on something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars

58:19.ar: ٱسۡتَحۡوَذَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ ذِكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
58:19.en: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they will be the losers

58:20.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَذَلِّينَ
58:20.en: Indeed, the ones who oppose Allah and His Messenger - those will be among the most humbled

58:21.ar: كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغۡلِبَنَّ أَنَا۠ وَرُسُلِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزࣱ‏
58:21.en: Allah has written, "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might

58:22.ar: لَّا تَجِدُ قَوۡمࣰ ا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ يُوَآدُّونَ مَنۡ حَآدَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَلَوۡ كَانُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنَهُمۡ أَوۡ عَشِيرَتَهُمۡۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَأَيَّدَهُم بِرُوحࣲ مِّنۡهُۖ وَيُدۡخِلُهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱللَّهِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
58:22.en: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him - those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah - they are the successful

ucDGF5XgqQM.title: Surat Al-Mujadilah Summary
ucDGF5XgqQM.one_line: Opening the Juz 28 cluster, Al-Mujadilah organizes relations among Muslims: ending zihar, secret councils, exclusion and misplaced loyalty.
ucDGF5XgqQM.summary: He starts a new cluster: the Medinan surahs of Juz 28, which organize Muslim society, covering spouses, gatherings, leaders, allies, enemies and unity. Al-Mujadilah deals with relations among Muslims. It opens with Khawlah, whose husband declared zihar, saying she was to him like his mother, a pre-Islamic trick that left a wife neither married nor divorced. She argued her case with the Prophet, Allah heard her, and the ruling abolished the practice and imposed an expiation. The first habit removed from the new society was the oppression of wives. Allah counts every deed even when people forget, and is the fourth of any three who talk in secret. Drawing on long experience, he calls secret councils the surest way to ruin a community: side meetings breed sin, alliances and hatred, and leave others feeling excluded. Private talk should be about good, and criticism belongs in the open meeting. Making room in gatherings means every Muslim has a place, whatever their background. Giving charity before a private consultation with the Prophet protected his time and funded society, a better model than constant fundraising. The surah ends by placing loyalty first with Muslims, warning against lying to oneself and then to Allah, and denying support to those who fight Allah and His Messenger, even close kin.

outline.heading: The Qaf to Al-Hadid cluster recapped
outline.gist: A run through the comparisons: purpose, guidance, knowledge, blessings, the three groups, and the balance between spirit and matter.

outline.heading: Juz 28: organizing Muslim society
outline.gist: These Medinan surahs organize relations with one another, non-Muslims, allies, enemies, spouses, families and leaders.

outline.heading: Al-Mujadilah: relations among Muslims
outline.gist: The surah removes pre-Islamic habits that cause oppression and hatred and sets priorities straight.

outline.heading: Khawlah and the practice of zihar
outline.gist: Her husband said she was to him like his mother, meaning no marital relations.

outline.heading: Zihar as a tool to oppress wives
outline.gist: It left a woman neither married nor divorced; Khawlah knew it could not stand in Islam and went to the Prophet.

outline.heading: She disputed, and Allah heard
outline.gist: She argued with the Prophet instead of waiting, and Allah heard the exchange and sent the ruling.

outline.heading: The expiation and the end of the first bad habit
outline.gist: Zihar became a sin requiring expiation; the oppression of wives in their homes was the first habit removed.

outline.heading: Allah counted it though they forgot
outline.gist: Everything is recorded in detail, including what we have forgotten.

outline.heading: No three confer but He is the fourth
outline.gist: Nothing said in secret is hidden from Allah; the verses turn to secret councils.

outline.heading: Secret councils ruin communities
outline.gist: If you want to destroy relationships, progress or a community, break off into side meetings after the general one.

outline.heading: Confer in righteousness; raise concerns openly
outline.gist: Private talk should be about good, and anything negative belongs in the larger meeting.

outline.heading: Secret talk wounds those left out
outline.gist: Cliques at school and work make others feel excluded and targeted; that is why it is sinful.

outline.heading: Interlude
Make room in gatherings
outline.gist: When asked to make space, do so for anyone, whatever their family, city, lineage or class.

outline.heading: Every Muslim has a place
outline.gist: Islam ended the practice of elders deciding who may enter; everyone's input is valuable.

outline.heading: Respecting the leader's time
outline.gist: Everyone wanted private time with the Prophet, and he was too kind to refuse, which exhausted him.

outline.heading: Charity before private consultation
outline.gist: Giving charity before a private talk reduced demands on the Prophet and brought wealth into society.

outline.heading: A better way to fund the community
outline.gist: Built-in giving instead of constant appeals that tire people and finish nothing.

outline.heading: Allying with those who are not of you
outline.gist: The verses criticize those who seek alliances with people under Allah's wrath.

outline.heading: Your alliances begin with Muslims
outline.gist: Your friendships, spending and direction should strengthen the Muslim community first.

outline.heading: Lying to yourself, then to Allah
outline.gist: Some lie to themselves until they believe it and will swear falsely before Allah.

outline.heading: No loyalty to those who fight Allah, even kin
outline.gist: Believers do not support those at war with Allah and His Messenger, even fathers, sons or brothers; he recaps the surah's rules.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The surah organizes relations among Muslims so the new society avoids oppression, hatred and division.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Zihar abolished as a way of oppressing wives.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Khawlah's courage in pressing for justice in her own home.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Allah has counted what people forget.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Secret councils breed hatred and leave others feeling targeted.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Every Muslim has a place in the gathering regardless of lineage or status.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Respecting the leader's time, and funding the community through structure rather than constant appeals.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: Loyalty and alliances belong first to the Muslim community.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Those who lie to themselves end up lying to Allah.

maxims: If you want to ruin a community, hold secret councils.
Anything negative belongs in the larger meeting.
Every Muslim has a place amongst us.

stories.point: A woman who knew Islam's values argued for justice, and Allah answered her by abolishing an oppressive custom.

stories.who: Companions seeking private time with the Prophet
stories.point: Leaders' time must be respected, and the charity rule served both the Prophet and society.

contemporary: Cliques and side meetings at school, work and in community organizations
Constant fundraising appeals in Muslim communities
takeaways: Never use words or customs that oppress your spouse.
Avoid side councils; raise concerns openly in the full meeting.
Make room for everyone in your gatherings, whatever their background.
Respect the time of your leaders and imams.
Direct your loyalty, friendship and spending to strengthening your Muslim community.

56:2.en: There is, at its occurrence, no denial

56:3.en: It will bring down [some] and raise up [others]

56:4.en: When the earth is shaken with convulsion

56:5.en: And the mountains are broken down, crumbling

56:8.en: Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right

56:9.en: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left

56:11.en: Those are the ones brought near [to Allah]

56:13.en: A [large] company of the former peoples

56:14.en: And a few of the later peoples

56:16.en: Reclining on them, facing each other

56:17.en: There will circulate among them young boys made eternal

56:18.en: With vessels, pitchers and a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring

56:19.en: No headache will they have therefrom, nor will they be intoxicated

56:20.en: And fruit of what they select

56:21.en: And the meat of fowl, from whatever they desire

56:22.en: And [for them are] fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes

56:24.en: As reward for what they used to do

56:25.ar: لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغۡوࣰ ا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمًا
56:25.en: They will not hear therein ill speech or commission of sin

56:26.ar: إِلَّا قِيلࣰ ا سَلَٰمࣰ ا سَلَٰمࣰ ا

56:27.en: The companions of the right - what are the companions of the right

56:28.en: [They will be] among lote trees with thorns removed

56:35.en: Indeed, We have produced the women of Paradise in a [new] creation

56:37.en: Devoted [to their husbands] and of equal age

56:38.en: For the companions of the right [who are]

56:39.en: A company of the former peoples

56:40.en: And a company of the later peoples

56:41.en: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left

56:42.en: [They will be] in scorching fire and scalding water

56:43.en: And a shade of black smoke

56:45.en: Indeed they were, before that, indulging in affluence

56:46.en: And they used to persist in the great violation

56:47.ar: وَكَانُواْ يَقُولُونَ أَئِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ
56:47.en: And they used to say, "When we die and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected

56:49.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, the former and the later peoples

56:50.en: Are to be gathered together for the appointment of a known Day

56:51.en: Then indeed you, O those astray [who are] deniers

56:52.en: Will be eating from trees of zaqqum

56:53.en: And filling with it your bellies

56:54.en: And drinking on top of it from scalding water

56:55.en: And will drink as the drinking of thirsty camels

56:56.en: That is their accommodation on the Day of Recompense

56:57.en: We have created you, so why do you not believe

56:58.en: Have you seen that which you emit

56:59.en: Is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator

56:60.ar: نَحۡنُ قَدَّرۡنَا بَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوقِينَ
56:60.en: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone

56:61.ar: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمۡثَٰلَكُمۡ وَنُنشِئَكُمۡ فِي مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
56:61.en: In that We will change your likenesses and produce you in that [form] which you do not know

56:62.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتُمُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ فَلَوۡلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
56:62.en: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember

56:63.en: And have you seen that [seed] which you sow

56:64.en: Is it you who makes it grow, or are We the grower

56:65.ar: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ حُطَٰمࣰ ا فَظَلۡتُمۡ تَفَكَّهُونَ
56:65.en: If We willed, We could make it [dry] debris, and you would remain in wonder

56:68.en: And have you seen the water that you drink

56:69.ar: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنزَلۡتُمُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُزۡنِ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنزِلُونَ
56:69.en: Is it you who brought it down from the clouds, or is it We who bring it down

56:70.ar: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ أُجَاجࣰ ا فَلَوۡلَا تَشۡكُرُونَ
56:70.en: If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful

56:71.en: And have you seen the fire that you ignite

56:72.ar: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنشَأۡتُمۡ شَجَرَتَهَآ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنشِـُٔونَ
56:72.en: Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer

56:73.ar: نَحۡنُ جَعَلۡنَٰهَا تَذۡكِرَةࣰ وَمَتَٰعࣰ ا لِّلۡمُقۡوِينَ
56:73.en: We have made it a reminder and provision for the travelers

56:74.en: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great

56:75.en: Then I swear by the setting of the stars

56:76.en: And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - [most] great

56:77.en: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an

56:79.en: None touch it except the purified

56:80.en: [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds

56:81.en: Then is it to this statement that you are indifferent

56:82.en: And make [the thanks for] your provision that you deny [the Provider]

56:83.en: Then why, when the soul at death reaches the throat

56:84.en: And you are at that time looking on

56:85.ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبۡصِرُونَ
56:85.en: And Our angels are nearer to him than you, but you do not see

56:86.en: Then why do you not, if you are not to be recompensed

56:87.en: Bring it back, if you should be truthful

56:88.en: And if the deceased was of those brought near to Allah

56:89.en: Then [for him is] rest and bounty and a garden of pleasure

56:90.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ
56:90.en: And if he was of the companions of the right

56:91.en: Then [the angels will say], "Peace for you; [you are] from the companions of the right

56:92.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
56:92.en: But if he was of the deniers [who were] astray

56:93.en: Then [for him is] accommodation of scalding water

56:95.en: Indeed, this is the true certainty

56:96.en: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great

6jZYFgoP1EM.speaker: adnan
6jZYFgoP1EM.speaker_note: his daily surah-summary series at MWN; continues the comparison cluster
6jZYFgoP1EM.title: Surat Al-Waqi'ah Summary
6jZYFgoP1EM.one_line: Al-Waqi'ah replaces worldly status with Allah's criteria, sorting people into three groups, and points to belief, the Quran and death as the way.
6jZYFgoP1EM.summary: He notes that Al-Waqi'ah is much loved and widely recited, though popular claims about it have little evidence. Its comparison is about status. In this world people get a status score from wealth, degrees, profession, family name and even skin colour, and society sorts itself by class. When the Event befalls, it lowers some and raises others by a different standard: good deeds, nearness to Allah, values and worship. That is a comfort for those who had few opportunities in life. People will be in three groups: the foremost, the people of the right and the people of the left. The foremost are many from the early generations and few from the later ones, so reaching that rank today takes extra effort. He describes the delights of the first two groups and notes that two of the three groups succeed. The people of the left are there for three reasons: extravagant consumption, refusing to give to the needy, and clinging to the great lie of shirk and denial of resurrection. The last part of the surah gives the path: certainty about Allah through arguments about seed, crops, water and fire; honouring the Quran; and remembering death, which no one can turn back. He asks listeners to keep these three in front of them and aim for the first two groups.

outline.heading: A beloved surah and the myths around it
outline.gist: Part of the comparison cluster; widely recited, though popular claims about its benefits have little evidence.

outline.heading: When the Event befalls
outline.gist: Waqi'ah means something coming into reality: the Day of Judgment, which nothing can hold back.

outline.heading: How the world ranks people
outline.gist: Wealth, degrees, profession, family name and even skin colour give each person a status score and a class.

outline.heading: Abasing some, raising others
outline.gist: On that day worldly status does not carry over; rank depends on deeds, nearness to Allah, values and worship, a comfort for those denied opportunities.

outline.heading: Three groups: right, left and foremost
outline.gist: The words sound like a political race, but the criteria behind them are entirely different.

outline.heading: The foremost: many from the early, few from the later
outline.gist: Those brought nearest to Allah are mostly from earlier generations, so reaching that rank in our time takes extra effort.

outline.heading: The delights of the foremost
outline.gist: Couches, cups that do not intoxicate, fruit and meat, and nothing heard but peace.

outline.heading: The people of the right
outline.gist: Thornless lote trees, layered banana trees and fruit that is never forbidden.

outline.heading: Two of the three groups succeed
outline.gist: Only one group fares badly, which gives every listener reason for hope.

outline.heading: A large group from both eras; the people of the left
outline.gist: The people of the right come from early and later generations alike; then scorching wind, scalding water and black smoke.

outline.heading: Why the left are there
outline.gist: Extravagant consumption while others suffered, withholding the right of the needy, and persisting in the great lie of shirk and denial of resurrection.

outline.heading: Interlude
Comparison needs contrast
outline.gist: The harsh description of the third group sharpens the comparison; there are also differences between the first two groups for those who look.

outline.heading: Three keys, beginning with belief: the seed you emit
outline.gist: After the comparison the surah points to belief, the Quran and death; what part do you play in turning a drop into a person?

outline.heading: Crops, water and fire
outline.gist: You plant a seed but do not make it grow; you do not send the rain or understand how fire burns.

outline.heading: Certainty first
outline.gist: These arguments build certainty; without it nothing works, and life will expose the smallest doubt.

outline.heading: A noble Quran touched only by the pure
outline.gist: The oath by the positions of the stars; will you make denial your share of provision?

outline.heading: The soul at the throat
outline.gist: Return the soul if you can; belief, the Quran and death are the three things to keep before you.

outline.heading: Each group at death
outline.gist: The nearest go to rest and gardens of bliss, the people of the right send peace, the deniers go to scalding water and fire.

outline.heading: The certain truth: glorify your Lord
outline.gist: This is the highest certainty; glorify the name of your Lord so you may land in one of the first two groups.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The three groups on the Day of Judgment and what each receives.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Worldly status from wealth, class and skin colour counts for nothing when the Event comes.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Extravagant consumption and withholding from the needy put people among those on the left.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Arguments from creation build the certainty without which nothing works.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is noble and preserved; do not trade it away.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death is near and cannot be reversed, so be ready.

hadith.gist: Reports of special benefits from reciting Al-Waqi'ah, such as protection from poverty, which he says have little evidence

maxims: Whatever status you built in the dunya won't carry over.
Life will expose the smallest doubt in your heart.
Belief, Quran, death: keep them on your billboard.
contemporary: Socioeconomic status and class as the way modern society ranks people
takeaways: Measure yourself by deeds, values and closeness to Allah, not worldly status.
Put in extra effort to be among the foremost, who are few in later times.
Avoid extravagance and give the needy their right from your wealth.
Build certainty in Allah, honour the Quran and stay ready for death.

49:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيِ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
49:1.en: O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger but fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing

49:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَرۡفَعُوٓاْ أَصۡوَٰتَكُمۡ فَوۡقَ صَوۡتِ ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَلَا تَجۡهَرُواْ لَهُۥ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ كَجَهۡرِ بَعۡضِكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ أَن تَحۡبَطَ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
49:2.en: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech like the loudness of some of you to others, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not

49:3.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصۡوَٰتَهُمۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمۡتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمۡ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۚ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرٌ عَظِيمٌ
49:3.en: Indeed, those who lower their voices before the Messenger of Allah - they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and great reward

49:4.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلۡحُجُرَٰتِ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
49:4.en: Indeed, those who call you, [O Muhammad], from behind the chambers - most of them do not use reason

49:5.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ صَبَرُواْ حَتَّىٰ تَخۡرُجَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:5.en: And if they had been patient until you [could] come out to them, it would have been better for them. But Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

49:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن جَآءَكُمۡ فَاسِقُۢ بِنَبَإࣲ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْ أَن تُصِيبُواْ قَوۡمَۢا بِجَهَٰلَةࣲ فَتُصۡبِحُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلۡتُمۡ نَٰدِمِينَ
49:6.en: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful

49:7.ar: وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِۚ لَوۡ يُطِيعُكُمۡ فِي كَثِيرࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ لَعَنِتُّمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَزَيَّنَهُۥ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ وَٱلۡفُسُوقَ وَٱلۡعِصۡيَانَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلرَّٰشِدُونَ
49:7.en: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided

49:8.ar: فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَنِعۡمَةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
49:8.en: [It is] as bounty from Allah and favor. And Allah is Knowing and Wise

49:9.ar: وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱقۡتَتَلُواْ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ فَإِنۢ بَغَتۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا عَلَى ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰ فَقَٰتِلُواْ ٱلَّتِي تَبۡغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيٓءَ إِلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن فَآءَتۡ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَهُمَا بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَأَقۡسِطُوٓاْۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
49:9.en: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly

49:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
49:10.en: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy

49:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَسۡخَرۡ قَوۡمࣱ مِّن قَوۡمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَلَا نِسَآءࣱ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُنَّۖ وَلَا تَلۡمِزُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَلَا تَنَابَزُواْ بِٱلۡأَلۡقَٰبِۖ بِئۡسَ ٱلِٱسۡمُ ٱلۡفُسُوقُ بَعۡدَ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَتُبۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
49:11.en: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers

49:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعۡضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثۡمࣱۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغۡتَب بَّعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًاۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمۡ أَن يَأۡكُلَ لَحۡمَ أَخِيهِ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَكَرِهۡتُمُوهُۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:12.en: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

49:15.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَرۡتَابُواْ وَجَٰهَدُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَأَنفُسِهِمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
49:15.en: The believers are only the ones who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful

49:16.ar: قُلۡ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
49:16.en: Say, "Would you acquaint Allah with your religion while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things

49:17.ar: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيۡكَ أَنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسۡلَٰمَكُمۖ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنۡ هَدَىٰكُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
49:17.en: They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful

49:18.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
49:18.en: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seeing of what you do

2ORFNbmZIJY.speaker: adnan

2ORFNbmZIJY.title: Surat Al-Hujurat Summary
2ORFNbmZIJY.one_line: Al-Hujurat distils the Prophet's adab: nothing before Allah and His Messenger, respect, verifying news, reconciling, social manners and an anthem against racism.
2ORFNbmZIJY.summary: Al-Hujurat closes the cluster on the Prophet. Surat Muhammad made following him the measure of accepted deeds and Al-Fath showed those who followed; Al-Hujurat gives the adab he brought and how to deal with him. For its two and a half pages it is perhaps the densest surah in commands. The first and most important: put nothing before Allah and His Messenger; in any matter, first ask what the shari'ah says, something increasingly ignored today. Do not raise your voice above his; as with parents, disrespect lowers the one who shows it, and it can void deeds unnoticed. The bedouins calling from behind his chambers teach privacy and asking permission. Then the adab of news: verify before acting or changing your heart toward someone, and if you cannot verify, refuse to listen. The Messenger is among us through the values and manners he left. When believers fight, reconciling them is a duty because believers are brothers. Social manners follow: no mockery meant to belittle, no hidden digs or hurtful nicknames, avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting. Verse 13 is the Quran's anthem against racism: diversity of peoples is a beauty meant for mutual knowing, and honour is only by taqwa, yet racism persists even within villages and families. The surah ends warning against treating one's Islam as a favour to Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Do not put yourselves before Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: In any matter in life, what Allah and the Prophet say comes first.

outline.heading: Disregarding the Prophet's guidance is being normalised
outline.gist: Choosing what we like over what he taught was once frowned upon; today it is increasingly normal.

outline.heading: Do not raise your voices above the Prophet's
outline.gist: Those who lower their voices have hearts tested for taqwa; loudness can void deeds unnoticed.

outline.heading: Respect reflects on you, as with parents
outline.gist: Publicly disrespecting a parent lowers the child, not the parent; respecting the Prophet builds our own manners.

outline.heading: Calling out from behind the chambers
outline.gist: Had they waited for him to come out it would have been better for them.

outline.heading: The cluster's close: the Prophet's adab
outline.gist: Muhammad gave following him as the measure of deeds, Al-Fath the examples of followers, and Al-Hujurat the manners he brought.

outline.heading: The densest surah in commands
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah has more but is far longer; every command here is a matter of adab worth learning.

outline.heading: First ask what the shari'ah says
outline.gist: Never place Allah's word or the Prophet's after another idea; perhaps the most important command in the surah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr and Umar raise their voices
outline.gist: The two best nearly perished when they argued loudly before him; the Prophet does not need our respect, it is for our sake.

outline.heading: Privacy and asking permission
outline.gist: Bedouins woke him at midday calling his name; knock, wait and leave if not answered, and respect elders, scholars and teachers.

outline.heading: Bad manners is not following him
outline.gist: After two surahs on following, this one gives its substance; the Prophet was all adab.

outline.heading: Verify news before you act
outline.gist: Before acting, taking a stand or changing your heart toward a person over something you heard, make sure it is true, or you will regret it.

outline.heading: Allah made faith beloved to you
outline.gist: If the Prophet followed you in many matters you would suffer; faith was beautified in your hearts.

outline.heading: Reconcile two fighting groups of believers
outline.gist: Believers are brothers, so disputes between them must be resolved by others.

outline.heading: Mockery, suspicion, spying and backbiting
outline.gist: The surah lists the social sins that damage brotherhood, ending with eating a dead brother's flesh.

outline.heading: If you cannot verify it, do not listen
outline.gist: No time to check is no excuse to act on a report; refuse to hear it instead.

outline.heading: The Messenger is among us through his values
outline.gist: Literally among the companions, he is among us through the manners he left; without them what have we taken from him?

outline.heading: Reconciling is your business
outline.gist: People in conflict cannot fix it themselves; a Muslim cannot walk away saying it is not his concern.

outline.heading: No mockery, hidden digs or hurtful nicknames
outline.gist: Not friendly banter but ridicule meant to lower someone; he asks women too to watch this when speaking of each other.

outline.heading: Good opinion, no spying, no backbiting
outline.gist: Suspicion gains you nothing and good opinion is worship, except in decisive matters like marriage or trade.

outline.heading: Peoples and tribes made to know one another
outline.gist: Diversity of cultures and nations is to be celebrated; Islam does not make everyone look the same.

outline.heading: The noblest is the most mindful of Allah
outline.gist: After adab with Allah, the Prophet, news, disputes and society comes adab with all of humanity.

outline.heading: The Quran's anthem against racism
outline.gist: All humans come from one male and female; differences of colour, language and custom are beauty, not grounds for superiority.

outline.heading: Racism in our own lands and families
outline.gist: Hateful racism persists even within one village, city or family, contradicting all the Prophet brought.

outline.heading: Do not count your Islam as a favour to Allah
outline.gist: The bedouins said they believed when they had only submitted; it is Allah who favours you by guiding you.

outline.heading: Outro
